question.problem: Express $\log_3\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)$ as a difference of logarithms.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the quotient rule for logarithms:

$$
\log_n(a) - \log_n(b) = \log_n\left( \dfrac{a}{b} \right)
$$

Using the quotient rule for logarithms, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{2}{5}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(2)-{log}_{3}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$
